correctness.rationale: The proof identifies each bidirected-star complex as the crown graph with t(t-1) edges, analyzes the base join C_a*C_b, and computes each of the two arrow links as K_{a,b}. For min(a,b)=1 the links are contractible; for min(a,b)=2 and max>2 the base is simply connected, and the cone inclusions are null-homotopic. For (a,b)=(2,2) one link maps by a homotopy equivalence to the base circle, so successive cofibres give a sphere; for both parameters >=3 the base is a wedge of 3-spheres and cone attachments contribute two sets of 2-spheres. Integral homotopy types imply torsion-free homology. An independently implemented chain routine enumerates all faces and signed boundaries and confirms predicted mod-2, mod-3, mod-5 reduced Betti numbers for all 21 unordered pairs with a,b <=6; it checks both central-arrow links. The finite experiment is not used as a universal homotopy certificate.

value.rationale: The result fills a motivated gap between the 2026 classification of bidirected linear graphs and the first symmetric trees with two independent branchings. It gives the complete integral homotopy type for every positive pair (a,b), exhibits a sharp transition from a circle or a single-dimensional sphere wedge to nontrivial homology in two adjacent degrees, and supplies exact unbounded multiplicities. The natural family is defined by the two branch counts of a double-star tree; the formulas are not arbitrary slices or isolated small computations. The mixed-dimensional base case a=b=3 and the exceptional boundary a=b=2 distinguish structures not determined by known path sphere results.
